title: Larry with a young Vietnamese soldier on the mountain
description: Larry stands among granite boulders with his arm around the shoulders of a smiling young Vietnamese soldier who cradles a Thompson-type submachine gun. Larry's name tape — HUNNEWELL — is fully legible, with a U.S. ARMY tape on the opposite chest and a white shield-shaped patch at his left pocket. Behind them, sandbags are stacked among boulders bearing painted Vietnamese inscriptions in red, and heavy cables run down the rock face to a dark equipment cabinet — powered equipment installed among the rocks.
researchNotes: Larry confirmed in conversation with his son (2026-08-17) that this is him. The survey had read the HUNNEWELL name tape as machine-level identification; his own word now anchors the identity thread the rest of the collection builds on, alongside his 2026-08-15 self-identifications in VN-0015 and VN-0022. Still open from this frame: the young soldier's name (he closely resembles the young man of VN-0009, same site), the contents of the equipment cabinet (radio/relay hypothesis), the white shield pocket patch (a re-scan target), and the painted rock inscriptions. The setting matches VN-0009/VN-0006 — the hypothesized Núi Bà Đen summit installation — but the site name remains unconfirmed by Larry, so no location is set here yet.
